quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. Do not turn around where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist's cushion of space change?

options.text: It should always stay the same.
It should change based on riding conditions.
It is not needed in most situations.
It should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy. Increase your following distance in these situations.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Cars pulling away from parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling away from parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, watch for vehicles pulling into traffic or leaving parking spaces.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: Riding a motorcycle is ______ driving a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: more tiring than
questions.explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car, especially on long trips. Do not ride when tired. Fatigue can make it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal when you finish a turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers about what you plan to do next.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (or orange in work zones). They warn you about hazards ahead or areas with special rules.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden moves on slippery surfaces. Any quick change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Move smoothly when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: You may not need extra space between you and the vehicle ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space behind other vehicles in bad conditions. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles most often conflict. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: Flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will slow down where drivers may not expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down where drivers may not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicle brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in places drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road safely and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When riding with other motorcyclists in a staggered formation:

options.text: Do not use it when entering or exiting a highway.
Use it when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use it when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce injury risk in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide real protection.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you feel a change, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes. Both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter. The brake applies when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes. Both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake right away.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear tire on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely. On good pavement with the motorcycle upright and going straight, you can control the motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What should motorcycle boots or shoes do?

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable material that resists slipping.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you always avoid?

options.text: The left part of the lane.
The center part of the lane.
The right part of the lane.
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: What is true about riding at night?

options.text: Wearing reflective clothing makes it safer.
It is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
It should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing reflective clothing makes it safer.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night. This makes other drivers more likely to see you on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to make yourself more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to make yourself more visible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a way that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Do not sit in a position that requires your arms to support your body weight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay on the right side of the road to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space around your motorcycle?

options.text: To prevent distractions from other vehicles.
To give yourself time to react to unexpected situations.
To keep traffic flowing at a steady pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position choices. You should pick the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it won't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, hold the handgrips firmly to keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to daytime?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day or night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It's hard to judge distances at night because you can't see shadows and light contrasts. Allow more space between you and the vehicle ahead at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: Your knees should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance when turning.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a flat tire. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is a better sign of tire failure.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't matter much since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
Should only be used when other vehicles are nearby.
Are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are vulnerable. Always use turn signals to let others know your plans. Use them whenever you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks only from a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip tighter and speed up to get past the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.
